children: The five days from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday are forecast to set another spending record when combining stores and online activity. Adobe expects retail sales during Cyber Week to be up 7.4% year over year to $47.5B, representing 17.3% of the full holiday season spend. Meanwhile, eMarketer forecasts that Cyber Five retail e-commerce sales will grow 7.3% this year, accounting for 16.5% of online holiday spending. Salesforce
, which measures a longer week starting November 24, predicts Cyber Week online sales will rise 6% to $84B.
A major factor lately has been that holiday shopping continues to be pulled even further forward on the calendar to October as Amazon

hold major sales events in October. Still, the National Retail Federation noted Thanksgiving weekend remains an important shopping event for shoppers searching for deals. Notably, Gen Z is the likeliest source of any upside. Salesforce
found 1 in 3 Gen Z shoppers (ages 14 to 29) plan to visit a store for Black Friday promotions, and 63% of Gen Z shoppers plan to shop in-store this holiday season. Separately, Uber

data cited by BTIG show teen mall trips up 50% from April, in a clear sign of momentum for the younger part of the demographic. The reason for the upturn? For many Gen Z shoppers, going to a store is a social outing that they still remember fondly from before the pandemic, rather than an errand.
